---
title: "Malle ERW Bayesian Treatment Comparison Plots"
subtitle: "Plots regenerated from existing Bayesian posterior contrasts"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    number-sections: true
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
  results: hide
---

Bayesian regression models were fitted separately for each soil physicochemical, mineralogical, aggregate stability, carbon and radiocarbon response variable using Stan via the cmdstanr package in R. Treatment-specific location parameters were estimated using a Student-t likelihood (with four degrees of freedom), with standardized response variables modelled as a function of treatment. Regularizing normal priors (μ ~ Normal(0, 1)) were assigned to treatment-specific parameters, while a half-Student-t prior was used for the residual standard deviation. Posterior distributions were estimated using four Markov chain Monte Carlo chains, with 2,000 warm-up and 2,000 sampling iterations per chain. Treatment effects were evaluated through posterior contrasts, calculated as differences between treatment-specific posterior estimates. Primary contrasts compared each amendment treatment (lime, Hühnerberg, Eifelgold and Bolsdorfer at 50 t ha⁻¹) against the untreated control. Posterior median differences and 95% credible intervals were calculated in both standardized and original measurement units. The posterior probability of a positive or negative treatment effect was determined as the proportion of posterior draws in which the corresponding treatment-control contrast was greater or less than zero, respectively.
No statistical comparisons were conducted for dose-response experiment (no replicates).

## Results

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide

# =============================================================================
# MALLE ERW: REGENERATE BAYESIAN TREATMENT COMPARISON PLOTS
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   - This is a plotting-only script.
#   - It does NOT fit or refit any Bayesian models.
#   - It loads existing CSV inputs and posterior contrast results.
#
# HTML output (plots are displayed inline; no files are saved):
#   1. Primary treatment-versus-Control forest plots
#   2. All-pairwise treatment forest plots
#   3. Grouped violin plots
#   4. Grouped Huhnerberg dose-response plots
#
# Forest plots:
#   Posterior treatment-minus-Control differences in standardized units,
#   with 95% credible intervals.
#
# Violin and dose-response plots:
#   Original measured values.
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# 1. PACKAGES
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(readr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(purrr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stringr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tibble))


# =============================================================================
# 2. DIRECTORIES AND INPUT FILES
# =============================================================================

# Explicit project root supplied by the user. This avoids here::here()
# resolving the project to C:/Users/tnel when the QMD is rendered elsewhere.
project_root <- "C:/Users/tnel/OneDrive - Universiteit Antwerpen/Documents/rocmics"

outputs_dir <- file.path(project_root, "outputs")

bayesian_treatment_out_dir <- file.path(
  outputs_dir,
  "Bayesian_treatment_comparisons"
)

integrated_file <- file.path(
  outputs_dir,
  "integrated_geochemistry_for_bayesian.csv"
)

primary_file <- file.path(
  bayesian_treatment_out_dir,
  "Bayesian_primary_basalt_vs_Control_Lime.csv"
)

pairwise_file <- file.path(
  bayesian_treatment_out_dir,
  "Bayesian_all_pairwise_treatment_contrasts.csv"
)



# Check that essential files exist

required_files <- c(
  integrated_file,
  primary_file,
  pairwise_file
)

missing_files <- required_files[!file.exists(required_files)]

if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The following required files could not be found:\n",
    paste(missing_files, collapse = "\n")
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 3. LOAD EXISTING DATA AND RESULTS
# =============================================================================

integrated <- read_csv(
  integrated_file,
  na = c("", "NA", "#VALUE!"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

primary_contrasts <- read_csv(
  primary_file,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

pairwise_contrasts <- read_csv(
  pairwise_file,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. TREATMENT DEFINITIONS
# =============================================================================

bayesian_treatment_levels <- c(
  "Control",
  "Lime",
  "HB 50",
  "EG 50",
  "BD 50"
)


# Reconstruct the same treatment selection used in the original analysis.

bayesian_treatment_data <- integrated %>%
  filter(
    Treatment == "Control" |
      grepl("^Lime", Treatment) |
      Treatment %in% c(
        "Huhnerberg_50",
        "Eifelgold_50",
        "Bolsdorfer_50"
      )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment_PCA = case_when(
      Treatment == "Control" ~ "Control",
      grepl("^Lime", Treatment) ~ "Lime",
      Treatment == "Huhnerberg_50" ~ "HB 50",
      Treatment == "Eifelgold_50" ~ "EG 50",
      Treatment == "Bolsdorfer_50" ~ "BD 50",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Treatment_PCA)) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment_PCA = factor(
      Treatment_PCA,
      levels = bayesian_treatment_levels
    )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 5. DEFINE PLOT GROUPS
# =============================================================================
#
# Each group produces:
#   - one primary forest plot
#   - one all-pairwise forest plot
#   - one violin plot
#   - one dose-response plot, where dose-response data are available
#
# Carbon stocks and radiocarbon signatures are combined so that each SOM
# fraction can be compared across C stocks and d14C.
#
# The four Tessier extractants are kept separate.
# =============================================================================

plot_groups <- list(

  Soil_Chemistry = c(
    "soil_pH",
    "soil_EC"
  ),

  Aggregate_Stability = c(
    "GMD_h2o",
    "D_h2o",
    "MWD_h2o",
    "GMD_oxalate_over_h2o",
    "D_oxalate_over_h2o",
    "MWD_oxalate_over_h2o"
  ),

  CEC_Cations = c(
    "CEC_CEC",
    "CEC_Base_saturation",
    "CEC_H",
    "CEC_Ca",
    "CEC_K",
    "CEC_Mg",
    "CEC_Na",
    "CEC_Al",
    "CEC_Fe",
    "CEC_Mn"
  ),

  Oxalate_DCB_Ratios = c(
    "Fe_ox_over_DCB",
    "Al_ox_over_DCB",
    "Mn_ox_over_DCB",
    "Si_ox_over_DCB",
    "Fe_ox_over_Si_ox",
    "Al_ox_over_Si_ox"
  ),

  Tessier_Carbonate = c(
    "Tessier_Acetic_Ca_mg_g",
    "Tessier_Acetic_K_mg_g",
    "Tessier_Acetic_Na_mg_g",
    "Tessier_Acetic_Mg_mg_g"
  ),

  Tessier_Exchangeable = c(
    "Tessier_NH4OAc_Ca_mg_g",
    "Tessier_NH4OAc_K_mg_g",
    "Tessier_NH4OAc_Na_mg_g",
    "Tessier_NH4OAc_Mg_mg_g"
  ),

  Tessier_Oxidizable = c(
    "Tessier_H2O2_Fe_mg_g",
    "Tessier_H2O2_Al_mg_g",
    "Tessier_H2O2_Mn_mg_g",
    "Tessier_H2O2_Si_mg_g"
  ),

  Tessier_Reducible = c(
    "Tessier_Hydroxylamine_Fe_mg_g",
    "Tessier_Hydroxylamine_Al_mg_g",
    "Tessier_Hydroxylamine_Mn_mg_g",
    "Tessier_Hydroxylamine_Si_mg_g"
  ),

  FTIR_Spectral = c(
    "FTIR_delta_aromatic",
    "FTIR_delta_Carbonate_bend",
    "FTIR_delta_carbonate_stretch",
    "FTIR_delta_carbonyl",
    "FTIR_delta_Aliphatic_total",
    "FTIR_delta_COO_total",
    "FTIR_delta_polysaccharide",
    "FTIR_delta_poorly_crystalline",
    "FTIR_delta_Silicate",
    "FTIR_delta_total_area"
  ),

  Carbon_and_Radiocarbon = c(
    "C_Bulk",
    "C_MAOM",
    "C_oPOM",
    "C_fPOM",
    "d14C_2026_Bulk",
    "d14C_2026_MAOM",
    "d14C_2026_oPOM",
    "d14C_2026_fPOM"
  )
)


# Retain only response variables actually present in the integrated dataset.

plot_groups_available <- lapply(
  plot_groups,
  function(x) {
    intersect(x, names(bayesian_treatment_data))
  }
)

# Remove empty groups.

plot_groups_available <- plot_groups_available[
  lengths(plot_groups_available) > 0
]


# =============================================================================
# 6. CHECK AND PREPARE POSTERIOR CONTRAST TABLES
# =============================================================================

required_primary_columns <- c(
  "Response",
  "Treatment_1",
  "Treatment_2",
  "Difference_standardized",
  "Lower_95_standardized",
  "Upper_95_standardized"
)

required_pairwise_columns <- required_primary_columns


missing_primary_columns <- setdiff(
  required_primary_columns,
  names(primary_contrasts)
)

missing_pairwise_columns <- setdiff(
  required_pairwise_columns,
  names(pairwise_contrasts)
)

if (length(missing_primary_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing columns in primary contrast CSV: ",
    paste(missing_primary_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

if (length(missing_pairwise_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing columns in pairwise contrast CSV: ",
    paste(missing_pairwise_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


# Primary comparisons must all be treatment minus Control.

primary_contrasts <- primary_contrasts %>%
  filter(
    Treatment_2 == "Control",
    Treatment_1 %in% c("Lime", "HB 50", "EG 50", "BD 50")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment_1 = factor(
      Treatment_1,
      levels = c("Lime", "HB 50", "EG 50", "BD 50")
    ),
    Comparison = paste(as.character(Treatment_1), "minus Control")
  )


# Keep the original comparison labels for the all-pairwise results.

pairwise_contrasts <- pairwise_contrasts %>%
  mutate(
    Comparison = if ("Comparison" %in% names(.)) {
      Comparison
    } else {
      paste(Treatment_1, "minus", Treatment_2)
    }
  )


# =============================================================================
# 7. CONVERT RAW DATA TO LONG FORMAT FOR VIOLIN PLOTS
# =============================================================================

# IMPORTANT:
#   Build a plain character vector of existing response columns.
#   This avoids the pivot_longer()/any_of() error.

plot_responses <- unique(
  unlist(plot_groups_available, use.names = FALSE)
)

plot_responses <- intersect(
  plot_responses,
  names(bayesian_treatment_data)
)

if (length(plot_responses) == 0) {
  stop("No plot response variables were found in bayesian_treatment_data.")
}


raw_data_plot <- bayesian_treatment_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(plot_responses),
    names_to = "Response",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Value) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment_PCA = factor(
      Treatment_PCA,
      levels = bayesian_treatment_levels
    ),
    Response = as.character(Response)
  )


# =============================================================================
# 8. HELPER: DISPLAY GROUPED FOREST PLOTS
# =============================================================================

make_grouped_forest_plot <- function(
    data,
    responses,
    group_name,
    comparison_type = "Primary") {

  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(Response %in% responses) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(Difference_standardized),
      is.finite(Lower_95_standardized),
      is.finite(Upper_95_standardized)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Response = factor(
        Response,
        levels = responses
      )
    )

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    message(
      "Skipping forest plot: ",
      group_name,
      " (no contrast data)"
    )
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Order comparisons consistently.

  if (comparison_type == "Primary") {

    comparison_levels <- c(
      "Lime minus Control",
      "HB 50 minus Control",
      "EG 50 minus Control",
      "BD 50 minus Control"
    )

  } else {

    comparison_levels <- unique(plot_data$Comparison)

  }

  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    mutate(
      Comparison = factor(
        Comparison,
        levels = rev(comparison_levels)
      )
    )

  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = Difference_standardized,
      y = Comparison
    )
  ) +

    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "grey45",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +

    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        xmin = Lower_95_standardized,
        xmax = Upper_95_standardized
      ),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.18,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +

    geom_point(
      size = 2.2
    ) +

    facet_wrap(
      ~ Response,
      ncol = 2,
      scales = "free_y"
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste(
        comparison_type,
        "Treatment Contrasts:",
        gsub("_", " ", group_name)
      ),
      subtitle = paste(
        "Posterior treatment differences in standardized units;",
        "points show posterior means and lines show 95% credible intervals"
      ),
      x = "Treatment difference (standardized units)",
      y = NULL
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "grey92",
        colour = "grey40"
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 9
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 13
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines")
    )

  n_responses <- length(unique(plot_data$Response))

  plot_height <- max(
    4.5,
    ceiling(n_responses / 2) * 2.8
  )

  print(p)

  return(p)
}


# =============================================================================
# 9. HELPER: DISPLAY GROUPED VIOLIN PLOTS
# =============================================================================

make_grouped_violin_plot <- function(
    data,
    responses,
    group_name) {

  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(Response %in% responses) %>%
    filter(is.finite(Value)) %>%
    mutate(
      Response = factor(
        Response,
        levels = responses
      ),
      Treatment_PCA = factor(
        Treatment_PCA,
        levels = bayesian_treatment_levels
      )
    )

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    message(
      "Skipping violin plot: ",
      group_name,
      " (no raw data)"
    )
    return(NULL)
  }

  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = Treatment_PCA,
      y = Value,
      fill = Treatment_PCA
    )
  ) +

    geom_violin(
      alpha = 0.65,
      trim = FALSE,
      scale = "width",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +

    geom_boxplot(
      width = 0.12,
      colour = "black",
      alpha = 0.8,
      outlier.shape = NA,
      linewidth = 0.35,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +

    facet_wrap(
      ~ Response,
      scales = "free_y",
      ncol = 2
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste(
        "Treatment Distributions:",
        gsub("_", " ", group_name)
      ),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Measured value"
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "grey92",
        colour = "grey40"
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 9
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 35,
        hjust = 1,
        size = 8
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 13
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines")
    )

  n_responses <- length(unique(plot_data$Response))

  plot_height <- max(
    5,
    ceiling(n_responses / 2) * 3
  )

  print(p)

  return(p)
}


# =============================================================================
# 10. GENERATE PRIMARY FOREST PLOTS
# =============================================================================

for (group_name in names(plot_groups_available)) {
  make_grouped_forest_plot(
    data = primary_contrasts,
    responses = plot_groups_available[[group_name]],
    group_name = group_name,
    comparison_type = "Primary"
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 11. GENERATE ALL-PAIRWISE FOREST PLOTS
# =============================================================================

for (group_name in names(plot_groups_available)) {
  make_grouped_forest_plot(
    data = pairwise_contrasts,
    responses = plot_groups_available[[group_name]],
    group_name = group_name,
    comparison_type = "All_Pairwise"
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 12. GENERATE GROUPED VIOLIN PLOTS
# =============================================================================

for (group_name in names(plot_groups_available)) {
  make_grouped_violin_plot(
    data = raw_data_plot,
    responses = plot_groups_available[[group_name]],
    group_name = group_name
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 13. HÜHNERBERG DOSE-RESPONSE DATA
# =============================================================================

hb_dose_data <- integrated %>%
  filter(
    Treatment == "Control" |
      grepl("^Huhnerberg", Treatment) |
      grepl("^HB_", Treatment) |
      grepl("^HB[0-9]", Treatment)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Dose_t_ha = case_when(
      Treatment == "Control" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ readr::parse_number(Treatment)
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Dose_t_ha)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(intersect(plot_responses, names(.))),
    names_to = "Response",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Value) %>%
  mutate(Response = as.character(Response))


# =============================================================================
# 14. HELPER: DISPLAY GROUPED DOSE-RESPONSE PLOTS
# =============================================================================

make_grouped_dose_plot <- function(
    data,
    responses,
    group_name) {

  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(Response %in% responses) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(Dose_t_ha),
      is.finite(Value)
    )

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    message(
      "Skipping dose-response plot: ",
      group_name,
      " (no observations)"
    )
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Summarise replicate values at each dose.
  # Points and error bars represent mean +/- SD.

  dose_summary <- plot_data %>%
    group_by(Response, Dose_t_ha) %>%
    summarise(
      Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = sum(!is.na(Value)),
      SE = SD / sqrt(n),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  p <- ggplot(
    dose_summary,
    aes(
      x = Dose_t_ha,
      y = Mean
    )
  ) +

    geom_line(
      linewidth = 0.7,
      colour = "darkblue"
    ) +

    geom_point(
      size = 2.2,
      colour = "darkblue"
    ) +

    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        ymin = Mean - SD,
        ymax = Mean + SD
      ),
      width = 0.5,
      linewidth = 0.45,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +

    facet_wrap(
      ~ Response,
      scales = "free_y",
      ncol = 2
    ) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = sort(unique(dose_summary$Dose_t_ha))
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste(
        "Hühnerberg Dose-Response:",
        gsub("_", " ", group_name)
      ),
      subtitle = "Mean +/- SD across replicate observations",
      x = "Hühnerberg application rate (t ha-1)",
      y = "Measured value"
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "grey92",
        colour = "grey40"
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 9
      ),
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 13
      ),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines")
    )

  n_responses <- length(unique(plot_data$Response))

  plot_height <- max(
    5,
    ceiling(n_responses / 2) * 3
  )

  print(p)

  return(p)
}


# =============================================================================
# 15. GENERATE GROUPED DOSE-RESPONSE PLOTS
# =============================================================================

for (group_name in names(plot_groups_available)) {
  make_grouped_dose_plot(
    data = hb_dose_data,
    responses = plot_groups_available[[group_name]],
    group_name = group_name
  )
}

```
